```python
def detect_rule_d(arcs, start_activities, end_activities):
    """
    Rule D: Loop Cut detection using graph partitioning.
    
    Algorithm:
    1. Initialize main group with all start and end activities
    2. Iteratively merge activities that violate edge rules
    3. Form redo groups from remaining activities
    4. Validate redo groups have proper loop connections
    5. Return (main_group, [redo_groups]) or None
    
    Returns:
        Tuple (main_group, list_of_redo_groups) if valid loop cut found, else None
    """
    
    # Get all unique activities
    all_activities = set()
    for a, b in arcs:
        all_activities.add(a)
        all_activities.add(b)
    
    if len(all_activities) < 2:
        return None
    
    # Build adjacency structures
    outgoing = {act: set() for act in all_activities}
    incoming = {act: set() for act in all_activities}
    
    for a, b in arcs:
        outgoing[a].add(b)
        incoming[b].add(a)
    
    # ============================================================
    # STEP 1: Initialize Main Group with all starts and ends
    # ============================================================
    main_group = set(start_activities | end_activities)
    
    if len(main_group) == 0:
        return None
    
    # ============================================================
    # STEP 2: Enforce Edge Rules (Iterative Merge)
    # ============================================================
    # Merge candidate into main if:
    # - Edge FROM main TO candidate does NOT originate from end activity, OR
    # - Edge FROM candidate TO main does NOT target start activity
    
    changed = True
    
    while changed:
        changed = False
        candidates = all_activities - main_group
        
        for candidate in candidates:
            should_merge = False
            
            # Check edges FROM main group TO candidate
            # If any edge does NOT originate from an end activity → merge
            incoming_from_main = incoming[candidate] & main_group
            for src in incoming_from_main:
                if src not in end_activities:
                    should_merge = True
                    break
            
            if not should_merge:
                # Check edges FROM candidate TO main group
                # If any edge does NOT target a start activity → merge
                outgoing_to_main = outgoing[candidate] & main_group
                for dst in outgoing_to_main:
                    if dst not in start_activities:
                        should_merge = True
                        break
            
            if should_merge:
                main_group.add(candidate)
                changed = True
    
    # ============================================================
    # STEP 3: Check Base Case
    # ============================================================
    # If all activities end up in main_group → return None
    if len(main_group) == len(all_activities):
        return None
    
    # ============================================================
    # STEP 4: Form Redo Groups (connected components)
    # ============================================================
    redo_candidates = all_activities - main_group
    
    # Build undirected adjacency within redo candidates
    redo_adjacency = {act: set() for act in redo_candidates}
    for a, b in arcs:
        if a in redo_candidates and b in redo_candidates:
            redo_adjacency[a].add(b)
            redo_adjacency[b].add(a)
    
    # Find connected components using BFS
    redo_visited = set()
    redo_groups = []
    
    for start_node in redo_candidates:
        if start_node not in redo_visited:
            group = set()
            queue = [start_node]
            
            while queue:
                node = queue.pop(0)
                if node not in redo_visited:
                    redo_visited.add(node)
                    group.add(node)
                    for neighbor in redo_adjacency[node]:
                        if neighbor not in redo_visited:
                            queue.append(neighbor)
            
            if len(group) > 0:
                redo_groups.append(group)
    
    # ============================================================
    # STEP 5: Validate Redo Groups
    # ============================================================
    # Each redo group needs:
    # - At least one incoming edge from an END activity of main_group
    # - At least one outgoing edge to a START activity of main_group
    
    main_end_activities = main_group & end_activities
    main_start_activities = main_group & start_activities
    
    valid_redo_groups = []
    activities_to_merge = set()
    
    for group in redo_groups:
        has_incoming_from_end = False
        has_outgoing_to_start = False
        
        for act in group:
            if not has_incoming_from_end:
                if len(incoming[act] & main_end_activities) > 0:
                    has_incoming_from_end = True
            
            if not has_outgoing_to_start:
                if len(outgoing[act] & main_start_activities) > 0:
                    has_outgoing_to_start = True
            
            if has_incoming_from_end and has_outgoing_to_start:
                break
        
        if has_incoming_from_end and has_outgoing_to_start:
            valid_redo_groups.append(group)
        else:
            activities_to_merge.update(group)
    
    # Merge invalid redo groups back into main
    if activities_to_merge:
        main_group.update(activities_to_merge)
    
    # ============================================================
    # STEP 6: Final Return
    # ============================================================
    if len(valid_redo_groups) == 0:
        return None
    
    # Validate loop connectivity
    has_enter_loop = any(a in main_group and b in redo_candidates for a, b in arcs)
    has_exit_loop = any(a in redo_candidates and b in main_group for a, b in arcs)
    
    if not (has_enter_loop and has_exit_loop):
        return None
    
    return (main_group, valid_redo_groups)
```

```python
def discover_process_tree(df_sublog, depth=0):

    activity_col = 'concept:name'

        return {"operator": "SILENT", "activity": "τ"}

    if len(all_activities) == 1:
        activity_name = list(all_activities)[0]
        
        if (activity_name, activity_name) in original_arcs:
            return {
                "operator": "D",
                "children": [
                    {"operator": "LEAF", "activity": activity_name},
                    {"operator": "SILENT", "activity": "τ"}
                ]
            }
        else:

    winning_rule = None
    rule_result = None
    
    result_a = detect_rule_a(original_arcs, start_activities, end_activities)
    if result_a is not None:
        winning_rule = 'A'
        rule_result = result_a
    
    if winning_rule is None:
        result_b = detect_rule_b(original_arcs, start_activities, end_activities)
        if result_b is not None:
            winning_rule = 'B'
            rule_result = result_b
    
    if winning_rule is None:
        result_c = detect_rule_c(original_arcs, start_activities, end_activities)
        if result_c is not None:
            winning_rule = 'C'
            rule_result = result_c
    
    if winning_rule is None:
        result_d = detect_rule_d(original_arcs, start_activities, end_activities)
        if result_d is not None:
            winning_rule = 'D'
            rule_result = result_d
    
    if winning_rule is None:
        working_arcs = set(original_arcs)
        max_arcs_to_remove = int(len(original_arcs) * 0.30)
        arcs_removed_count = 0
        
        while True:
            if arcs_removed_count >= max_arcs_to_remove or len(working_arcs) == 0:
                break
            
            if detect_rule_a(working_arcs, start_activities, end_activities) is not None:
                winning_rule = 'A'
                rule_result = detect_rule_a(working_arcs, start_activities, end_activities)
                break
            
            if detect_rule_b(working_arcs, start_activities, end_activities) is not None:
                winning_rule = 'B'
                rule_result = detect_rule_b(working_arcs, start_activities, end_activities)
                break
            
            if detect_rule_c(working_arcs, start_activities, end_activities) is not None:
                winning_rule = 'C'
                rule_result = detect_rule_c(working_arcs, start_activities, end_activities)
                break
            
            if detect_rule_d(working_arcs, start_activities, end_activities) is not None:
                winning_rule = 'D'
                rule_result = detect_rule_d(working_arcs, start_activities, end_activities)
                break
            
            min_freq = float('inf')
            min_arc = None
            
            for arc in working_arcs:
                freq = original_arc_freq.get(arc, 1)
                if freq < min_freq:
                    min_freq = freq
                    min_arc = arc
            
            if min_arc is not None:
                working_arcs = working_arcs - {min_arc}
                arcs_removed_count += 1
            else:
                break
    
    if winning_rule is None:
        return {"operator": "FLOWER", "activities": sorted(list(all_activities))}
    
    if winning_rule == 'A':
        groups = rule_result
        case_to_group = {}
        
        for case_id in df_sublog[case_col].unique():
            case_activities = set(df_sublog[df_sublog[case_col] == case_id][activity_col])
            best_group_idx = 0
            best_overlap = 0
            
            for i, group in enumerate(groups):
                overlap = len(case_activities & group)
                if overlap > best_overlap:
                    best_overlap = overlap
                    best_group_idx = i
            
            case_to_group[case_id] = best_group_idx
        
        child_sublogs = []
        for i, group in enumerate(groups):
            case_ids_for_group = [cid for cid, gidx in case_to_group.items() if gidx == i]
            sublog = df_sublog[df_sublog[case_col].isin(case_ids_for_group)].copy().reset_index(drop=True)
            child_sublogs.append(sublog)
        
        children = [discover_process_tree(sl, depth + 1) for sl in child_sublogs]
    
    elif winning_rule in ['B', 'C']:
        groups = rule_result
        child_sublogs = []
        for group in groups:
            sublog = df_sublog[df_sublog[activity_col].isin(group)].copy().reset_index(drop=True)
            child_sublogs.append(sublog)
        
        children = [discover_process_tree(sl, depth + 1) for sl in child_sublogs]
    
    elif winning_rule == 'D':
        main_group, return_groups = rule_result
        
        main_sublog = df_sublog[df_sublog[activity_col].isin(main_group)].copy().reset_index(drop=True)
        main_tree = discover_process_tree(main_sublog, depth + 1)
        
        if len(return_groups) == 1:
            return_sublog = df_sublog[df_sublog[activity_col].isin(return_groups[0])].copy().reset_index(drop=True)
            return_tree = discover_process_tree(return_sublog, depth + 1)
            children = [main_tree, return_tree]
        
        elif len(return_groups) >= 2:
            choice_children = []
            
            for return_group in return_groups:
                return_sublog = df_sublog[df_sublog[activity_col].isin(return_group)].copy().reset_index(drop=True)
                return_tree = discover_process_tree(return_sublog, depth + 1)
                choice_children.append(return_tree)
            
            redo_choice_node = {"operator": "A", "children": choice_children}
            children = [main_tree, redo_choice_node]
        
        else:
            children = [main_tree]
    
    parent_activities = all_activities
    
    split_invalid = False
    for child_tree in children:
        def get_tree_activities(tree):
            if tree["operator"] == "LEAF" or tree["operator"] == "SILENT":
                return {tree.get("activity", "")}
            elif tree["operator"] == "FLOWER":
                return set(tree["activities"])
            else:
                acts = set()
                for c in tree["children"]:
                    acts.update(get_tree_activities(c))
                return acts
        
        child_activities = get_tree_activities(child_tree)
        if child_activities == parent_activities:
            split_invalid = True
            break
    
    if split_invalid:
        return {"operator": "FLOWER", "activities": sorted(list(all_activities))}
    
    return {"operator": winning_rule, "children": children}


def print_process_tree(tree, indent=0):
    """
    Print a process tree with proper indentation.
    """
    prefix = "    " * indent
    
    if tree["operator"] == "LEAF":
        print(f"{prefix}· {tree['activity']}")
    
    elif tree["operator"] == "SILENT":
        print(f"{prefix}· τ")
    
    elif tree["operator"] == "FLOWER":
        activities_str = ", ".join(tree["activities"])
        print(f"{prefix}⊕ FLOWER({activities_str})")
    
    else:
        operator_names = {
            'A': '× (Exclusive Choice)',
            'B': '→ (Sequence)',
            'C': '∧ (Parallel)',
            'D': '⟳ (Loop)'
        }
        op_name = operator_names.get(tree["operator"], tree["operator"])
        print(f"{prefix}[{op_name}]")
        
        for child in tree["children"]:
            print_process_tree(child, indent + 1)
```

```python
import pandas as pd
import io
from collections import Counter
import pm4py


def parse_sample_data(raw_text):
    """
    Parse whitespace-separated raw text into a Pandas DataFrame.
    
    Uses manual line-by-line parsing to handle activity names with spaces.
    Splits each line on the FIRST whitespace only:
      - Part 1: case ID (no spaces)
      - Part 2: activity name (may contain spaces)
    
    Parameters:
        raw_text: String containing the raw event log data
    
    Returns:
        df: Pandas DataFrame with columns 'case:concept:name' and 'concept:name'
    """
    lines = raw_text.strip().split('\n')
    
    case_ids = []
    activities = []
    
    for line in lines[1:]:
        line = line.strip()
        
        if not line:
            continue
        
        parts = line.split(None, 1)
        
        case_id = parts[0]
        activity_name = parts[1] if len(parts) > 1 else ''
        
        case_ids.append(case_id)
        activities.append(activity_name)
    
    df = pd.DataFrame({
        'case:concept:name': case_ids,
        'concept:name': activities
    })
    
    return df


def load_real_log(file_path):
    """
    Load a real XES event log file using pm4py and convert to DataFrame.
    
    Only pm4py's read/convert functions are used here.
    NO discovery algorithms are called.
    
    Parameters:
        file_path: Path to the .xes or .xes.gz file
    
    Returns:
        df: Pandas DataFrame with standard XES column names
            ('case:concept:name' and 'concept:name')
    """
    # Read the .xes file into pm4py's internal format
    event_log = pm4py.read_xes(file_path)
    
    # Convert directly to Pandas DataFrame
    df = pm4py.convert_to_dataframe(event_log)
    
    # BPI logs use standard XES column names, so pm4py preserves them correctly
    # Common column names from pm4py:
    #   - 'case:concept:name' for case ID
    #   - 'concept:name' for activity name
    #   - 'time:timestamp' for event timestamp
    
    return df


def build_directly_follows_graph(df):
    """
    Build the directly-follows graph from the event log DataFrame.
    
    Uses ONLY vectorized Pandas operations - no row iteration.
    
    Parameters:
        df: Pandas DataFrame with columns 'case:concept:name' and 'concept:name'
            Rows must be in chronological order (as loaded from .xes file)
    
    Returns:
        arcs: set of tuples (A, B) where B directly follows A in some trace
        start_activities: set of activities that start traces
        end_activities: set of activities that end traces
    """
    
    case_col = 'case:concept:name'
    activity_col = 'concept:name'
    
    start_activities = set(df.groupby(case_col)[activity_col].first())
    end_activities = set(df.groupby(case_col)[activity_col].last())
    
    df_work = df.copy()
    df_work['next_activity'] = df_work[activity_col].shift(-1)
    df_work['next_case'] = df_work[case_col].shift(-1)
    
    same_case_mask = df_work[case_col] == df_work['next_case']
    df_valid_arcs = df_work[same_case_mask]
    
    arcs = set(zip(df_valid_arcs[activity_col], df_valid_arcs['next_activity']))
    
    return arcs, start_activities, end_activities


def build_directly_follows_graph_with_frequency(df):
    """
    Build DFG with arc frequencies for dynamic fallback.
    Returns: arcs (set), arc_freq (dict), start_activities, end_activities
    """
    case_col = 'case:concept:name'
    activity_col = 'concept:name'
    
    start_activities = set(df.groupby(case_col)[activity_col].first())
    end_activities = set(df.groupby(case_col)[activity_col].last())
    
    df_work = df.copy()
    df_work['next_activity'] = df_work[activity_col].shift(-1)
    df_work['next_case'] = df_work[case_col].shift(-1)
    
    same_case_mask = df_work[case_col] == df_work['next_case']
    df_valid = df_work[same_case_mask]
    
    arc_pairs = list(zip(df_valid[activity_col], df_valid['next_activity']))
    arc_freq = Counter(arc_pairs)
    
    arcs = set(arc_freq.keys())
    
    return arcs, dict(arc_freq), start_activities, end_activities
```

```python
import pandas as pd

      - Part 1: case ID (no spaces)

    Parameters:

    Returns:
        df: Pandas DataFrame with columns 'case:concept:name' and 'concept:name'
    """
    lines = raw_text.strip().split('\n')
    
    case_ids = []
    activities = []
    
    for line in lines[1:]:
        line = line.strip()
        
        if not line:

        parts = line.split(None, 1)
        
        case_id = parts[0]
        activity_name = parts[1] if len(parts) > 1 else ''
        
        case_ids.append(case_id)
        activities.append(activity_name)
    
    df = pd.DataFrame({
        'case:concept:name': case_ids,
        'concept:name': activities
    })
    
    return df


def load_real_log(file_path):
    """

    Only pm4py's read/convert functions are used here.
    NO discovery algorithms are called.
    
    Parameters:
        file_path: Path to the .xes or .xes.gz file
    
    Returns:
        df: Pandas DataFrame with standard XES column names
            ('case:concept:name' and 'concept:name')
    """

    event_log = pm4py.read_xes(file_path)

    # Common column names from pm4py:
    #   - 'case:concept:name' for case ID
    #   - 'concept:name' for activity name
    #   - 'time:timestamp' for event timestamp
    
    return df

    """
```
```python
    Internal helper function to filter out low-frequency activities and arcs.
    
    Steps:
    1. Calculate activity frequencies
    2. Keep activities with count >= threshold * max_activity_count
    3. Filter DataFrame to only rows with valid activities
    4. Calculate arc frequencies
    5. Keep arcs with count >= threshold * max_arc_frequency
    
    Parameters:
        df: Input DataFrame
        noise_threshold: Minimum frequency ratio (e.g., 0.02 = 2%)
    
    Returns:
        df_filtered: Filtered DataFrame
        valid_activities: Set of activities that passed the filter
        valid_arcs: Set of arcs that passed the filter
        arc_freq_filtered: Dictionary of arc frequencies (filtered)
    """

    activity_col = 'concept:name'
    
    # ============================================================
    # STEP 1: Global Activity Filter
    # ============================================================
    activity_counts = df[activity_col].value_counts()
    max_activity_count = activity_counts.max()
    min_activity_freq = noise_threshold * max_activity_count
    
    # Keep activities with frequency >= threshold
    valid_activities = set(activity_counts[activity_counts >= min_activity_freq].index)
    
    # Filter DataFrame to keep only rows with valid activities
    df_filtered = df[df[activity_col].isin(valid_activities)].copy().reset_index(drop=True)

    # ============================================================
    df_work = df_filtered.copy()
    df_work['next_activity'] = df_work[activity_col].shift(-1)
    df_work['next_case'] = df_work[case_col].shift(-1)
    
    same_case_mask = df_work[case_col] == df_work['next_case']
    df_valid = df_work[same_case_mask]
    
    # Calculate arc frequencies
    arc_pairs = list(zip(df_valid[activity_col], df_valid['next_activity']))
    arc_freq = Counter(arc_pairs)
    
    # ============================================================
    # STEP 3: Arc Filter
    # ============================================================
    if len(arc_freq) > 0:
        max_arc_frequency = max(arc_freq.values())
        min_arc_freq = noise_threshold * max_arc_frequency
        
        # Keep arcs with frequency >= threshold
        valid_arcs = {arc for arc, freq in arc_freq.items() if freq >= min_arc_freq}
        arc_freq_filtered = {arc: freq for arc, freq in arc_freq.items() if freq >= min_arc_freq}
    else:
        valid_arcs = set()
        arc_freq_filtered = {}
    
    return df_filtered, valid_activities, valid_arcs, arc_freq_filtered

    Uses ONLY vectorized Pandas operations - no row iteration.
    
    Parameters:

        noise_threshold: Minimum frequency ratio for activities/arcs (default 0.02 = 2%)

        start_activities: set of activities that start traces (from filtered data)
        end_activities: set of activities that end traces (from filtered data)
    """

    # Apply arc filter (only keep arcs that passed noise threshold)
    arcs = arcs_raw & valid_arcs if len(valid_arcs) > 0 else arcs_raw

    """

    df_work['next_activity'] = df_work[activity_col].shift(-1)
    df_work['next_case'] = df_work[case_col].shift(-1)
    
    same_case_mask = df_work[case_col] == df_work['next_case']
    df_valid = df_work[same_case_mask]
    
    arc_pairs = list(zip(df_valid[activity_col], df_valid['next_activity']))
    arc_freq_raw = Counter(arc_pairs)
    
    # Use pre-filtered frequencies if available, otherwise filter now
    if len(arc_freq_filtered) > 0:
        arc_freq = arc_freq_filtered
        arcs = set(arc_freq.keys())
    else:
        # Fallback: apply threshold manually
        if len(arc_freq_raw) > 0:
            max_arc_frequency = max(arc_freq_raw.values())
            min_arc_freq = noise_threshold * max_arc_frequency
            arc_freq = {arc: freq for arc, freq in arc_freq_raw.items() if freq >= min_arc_freq}
            arcs = set(arc_freq.keys())
        else:
            arc_freq = {}
            arcs = set()
    
    return arcs, arc_freq, start_activities, end_activities
```

```python
        - 'C' → AND (Parallel)
        - 'D' → LOOP (with main body and redo path)
        - 'LEAF' → Activity leaf node
        - 'SILENT' → Silent transition (τ)

    # Import operator constants
    from pm4py.objects.process_tree.obj import Operator
    
    operator = node.get("operator", "")
    
    # ============================================================
    # LEAF Node: Create activity node
    # ============================================================
    if operator == "LEAF":
        activity_name = node.get("activity", "unknown")
        pt_node = ProcessTree(activity_name)

            parent.children.append(pt_node)
            pt_node.parent = parent
        
        return pt_node
    
    # ============================================================
    # SILENT Node: Create silent transition (τ)
    # ============================================================
    elif operator == "SILENT":
        pt_node = ProcessTree(None)  # None represents silent transition
        
        if parent is not None:
            parent.children.append(pt_node)
            pt_node.parent = parent
        
        return pt_node
    
    # ============================================================
    # FLOWER Node: Approximate as XOR of all activities
    # ============================================================
    elif operator == "FLOWER":

        for activity in activities:

                child = ProcessTree(None)  # Silent
            else:
                child = ProcessTree(activity)
            pt_node.children.append(child)
            child.parent = pt_node
        
        return pt_node
    
    # ============================================================
    # Internal Operator Nodes (A, B, C, D)
    # ============================================================
    else:
        # Map our operators to pm4py operators
        operator_mapping = {
            'A': Operator.XOR,       # Exclusive Choice
            'B': Operator.SEQUENCE,  # Sequence
            'C': Operator.AND,       # Parallel
            'D': Operator.LOOP       # Loop
        }

        children = node.get("children", [])
```

```python
import json
```
from datetime import datetime
from collections import Counter


# ============================================================================
# 1. DATA EXTRACTION - Convert pm4py net to pure Python structures
# ============================================================================

def extract_net_structure(net):
    """
    Extract Petri net structure into pure Python dictionaries.
    
    Parameters:
        net: pm4py Petri net object
    
    Returns:
        input_arcs: dict mapping transitions to their input places
        output_arcs: dict mapping transitions to their output places
        place_to_transitions: dict mapping places to their output transitions
        silent_transitions: set of transition labels that are None (silent/τ)
        all_places: list of all place objects
        all_transitions: list of all transition objects
    """
    input_arcs = {}
    output_arcs = {}
    place_to_transitions = {}
    silent_transitions = set()
    
    # Initialize structures for all transitions
    for trans in net.transitions:
        input_arcs[trans] = []
        output_arcs[trans] = []
    
    # Extract arcs
    for arc in net.arcs:
        if hasattr(arc, 'source') and hasattr(arc, 'target'):
            source = arc.source
            target = arc.target
            
            # Place to Transition (input arc for transition)
            if source in net.places and target in net.transitions:
                input_arcs[target].append(source)
            
            # Transition to Place (output arc for transition)
            elif source in net.transitions and target in net.places:
                output_arcs[source].append(target)
    
    # Build place to transitions mapping
    for place in net.places:
        place_to_transitions[place] = []
        for trans in net.transitions:
            if place in input_arcs[trans]:
                place_to_transitions[place].append(trans)
    
    # Identify silent transitions (label is None)
    for trans in net.transitions:
        if trans.label is None:
            silent_transitions.add(trans)
    
    return {
        'input_arcs': input_arcs,
        'output_arcs': output_arcs,
        'place_to_transitions': place_to_transitions,
        'silent_transitions': silent_transitions,
        'all_places': list(net.places),
        'all_transitions': list(net.transitions)
    }


# ============================================================================
# 2. TOKEN-BASED REPLAY (FITNESS)
# ============================================================================

def enable_transitions(markings, net_struct):
    """
    Find all enabled transitions given current markings.
    
    A transition is enabled if all its input places have at least 1 token.
    Silent transitions are also included.
    
    Parameters:
        markings: dict mapping places to token counts
        net_struct: extracted net structure
    
    Returns:
        Set of enabled transitions
    """
    enabled = set()
    input_arcs = net_struct['input_arcs']
    
    for trans in net_struct['all_transitions']:
        input_places = input_arcs[trans]
        if all(markings.get(place, 0) > 0 for place in input_places):
            enabled.add(trans)
    
    return enabled


def fire_transition(markings, trans, net_struct):
    """
    Fire a transition: consume tokens from input places, produce to output places.
    
    Parameters:
        markings: dict mapping places to token counts (modified in place)
        trans: transition to fire
        net_struct: extracted net structure
    
    Returns:
        Updated markings dict
    """
    input_arcs = net_struct['input_arcs']
    output_arcs = net_struct['output_arcs']
    
    # Consume from input places
    for place in input_arcs[trans]:
        markings[place] = markings.get(place, 0) - 1
    
    # Produce to output places
    for place in output_arcs[trans]:
        markings[place] = markings.get(place, 0) + 1
    
    return markings


def fire_silent_transitions(markings, net_struct):
    """
    Fire all possible silent transitions until no more can fire.
    
    Parameters:
        markings: dict mapping places to token counts
        net_struct: extracted net structure
    
    Returns:
        Updated markings dict
    """
    silent = net_struct['silent_transitions']
    changed = True
    
    while changed:
        changed = False
        enabled = enable_transitions(markings, net_struct)
        
        for trans in enabled:
            if trans in silent:
                markings = fire_transition(markings, trans, net_struct)
                changed = True
                break  # Restart to check for newly enabled silent transitions
    
    return markings


def replay_trace(trace, net_struct, initial_marking_dict):
    """
    Replay a single trace through the Petri net.
    
    Tracks missing tokens (when activity not enabled) and remaining tokens.
    
    Parameters:
        trace: list of activity names
        net_struct: extracted net structure
        initial_marking_dict: dict mapping places to initial token counts
    
    Returns:
        missing_tokens: count of missing tokens
        remaining_tokens: count of tokens left after replay
        consumed: total tokens consumed
        produced: total tokens produced
    """
    markings = initial_marking_dict.copy()
    missing_tokens = 0
    consumed = 0
    produced = 0
    
    # Fire initial silent transitions
    markings = fire_silent_transitions(markings, net_struct)
    
    for activity in trace:
        # Find transitions with this label
        candidate_transitions = [
            t for t in net_struct['all_transitions']
            if t.label == activity
        ]
        
        # Check if any candidate is enabled
        enabled = enable_transitions(markings, net_struct)
        enabled_candidates = [t for t in candidate_transitions if t in enabled]
        
        if enabled_candidates:
            # Fire the first enabled matching transition
            trans = enabled_candidates[0]
            markings = fire_transition(markings, trans, net_struct)
            consumed += len(net_struct['input_arcs'][trans])
            produced += len(net_struct['output_arcs'][trans])
        else:
            # Activity not enabled - add missing token
            missing_tokens += 1
            
            # Force enable by adding token to a relevant place (heuristic)
            if candidate_transitions:

                for place in net_struct['input_arcs'][trans]:
                    if markings.get(place, 0) == 0:
                        markings[place] = 1
                        break
                
                # Now fire it
                markings = fire_transition(markings, trans, net_struct)
                consumed += len(net_struct['input_arcs'][trans])
                produced += len(net_struct['output_arcs'][trans])
        
        # Fire silent transitions after each activity
        markings = fire_silent_transitions(markings, net_struct)
    
    # Count remaining tokens
    remaining_tokens = sum(markings.values())
    
    return missing_tokens, remaining_tokens, consumed, produced


def calculate_fitness(df, net, initial_marking, final_marking):
    """
    Calculate token-based replay fitness.
    
    Fitness = 1 - ((missing_tokens + remaining_tokens) / (2 * total_activities))
    
    Parameters:
        df: pandas DataFrame with event log
        net: pm4py Petri net
        initial_marking: pm4py marking

    initial_marking_dict = {}
    for place, count in initial_marking.items():
        initial_marking_dict[place] = count
    
    # Group events by case
    case_col = 'case:concept:name'
    activity_col = 'concept:name'
    
    traces = []
    for case_id in df[case_col].unique():
        case_events = df[df[case_col] == case_id].sort_index()
        trace = case_events[activity_col].tolist()
        traces.append(trace)
    
    # Replay all traces
    total_missing = 0

```python
import json
from datetime import datetime


# ============================================================================
# 1. DATA EXTRACTION - Convert pm4py net to pure Python structures
# ============================================================================

def extract_net_structure(net):
    """
    Extract Petri net structure into pure Python dictionaries.
    """
    input_arcs = {}
    output_arcs = {}
    place_to_transitions = {}
    silent_transitions = set()
    
    # Initialize structures for all transitions
    for trans in net.transitions:
        input_arcs[trans] = []
        output_arcs[trans] = []
    
    # Extract arcs
    for arc in net.arcs:
        if hasattr(arc, 'source') and hasattr(arc, 'target'):
            source = arc.source
            target = arc.target
            
            if source in net.places and target in net.transitions:
                input_arcs[target].append(source)
            
            elif source in net.transitions and target in net.places:
                output_arcs[source].append(target)
    
    # Build place to transitions mapping
    for place in net.places:
        place_to_transitions[place] = []
        for trans in net.transitions:
            if place in input_arcs[trans]:
                place_to_transitions[place].append(trans)
    
    # Identify silent transitions
    for trans in net.transitions:
        if trans.label is None:
            silent_transitions.add(trans)
    
    return {
        'input_arcs': input_arcs,
        'output_arcs': output_arcs,
        'place_to_transitions': place_to_transitions,
        'silent_transitions': silent_transitions,
        'all_places': list(net.places),
        'all_transitions': list(net.transitions)
    }


# ============================================================================
# 2. TOKEN-BASED REPLAY (FITNESS)
# ============================================================================

def enable_transitions(markings, net_struct):
    """Find all enabled transitions given current markings."""
    enabled = set()
    input_arcs = net_struct['input_arcs']
    
    for trans in net_struct['all_transitions']:
        input_places = input_arcs[trans]
        if all(markings.get(place, 0) > 0 for place in input_places):
            enabled.add(trans)
    
    return enabled


def fire_transition(markings, trans, net_struct):
    """Fire a transition: consume tokens from input, produce to output."""
    input_arcs = net_struct['input_arcs']
    output_arcs = net_struct['output_arcs']
    
    for place in input_arcs[trans]:
        markings[place] = markings.get(place, 0) - 1
    
    for place in output_arcs[trans]:
        markings[place] = markings.get(place, 0) + 1
    
    return markings


def fire_silent_transitions(markings, net_struct):
    """Fire all possible silent transitions until no more can fire."""
    silent = net_struct['silent_transitions']
    changed = True
    
    while changed:
        changed = False
        enabled = enable_transitions(markings, net_struct)
        
        for trans in enabled:
            if trans in silent:
                markings = fire_transition(markings, trans, net_struct)
                changed = True
                break
    
    return markings


def replay_trace(trace, net_struct, initial_marking_dict):
    """Replay a single trace through the Petri net."""
    markings = initial_marking_dict.copy()
    missing_tokens = 0
    consumed = 0
    produced = 0
    
    markings = fire_silent_transitions(markings, net_struct)
    
    for activity in trace:
        candidate_transitions = [
            t for t in net_struct['all_transitions']
            if t.label == activity
        ]
        
        enabled = enable_transitions(markings, net_struct)
        enabled_candidates = [t for t in candidate_transitions if t in enabled]
        
        if enabled_candidates:
            trans = enabled_candidates[0]
            markings = fire_transition(markings, trans, net_struct)
            consumed += len(net_struct['input_arcs'][trans])
            produced += len(net_struct['output_arcs'][trans])
        else:
            missing_tokens += 1
            
            if candidate_transitions:
                trans = candidate_transitions[0]
                for place in net_struct['input_arcs'][trans]:
                    if markings.get(place, 0) == 0:
                        markings[place] = 1
                        break
                
                markings = fire_transition(markings, trans, net_struct)
                consumed += len(net_struct['input_arcs'][trans])
                produced += len(net_struct['output_arcs'][trans])
        
        markings = fire_silent_transitions(markings, net_struct)
    
    remaining_tokens = sum(markings.values())
    
    return missing_tokens, remaining_tokens, consumed, produced


def calculate_fitness_details(df, net, initial_marking, final_marking):
    """Calculate token-based replay fitness details."""
    net_struct = extract_net_structure(net)
    
    initial_marking_dict = {}
    for place, count in initial_marking.items():
        initial_marking_dict[place] = count
    
    case_col = 'case:concept:name'
    activity_col = 'concept:name'
    
    traces = []
    for case_id in df[case_col].unique():
        case_events = df[df[case_col] == case_id].sort_index()
        trace = case_events[activity_col].tolist()
        traces.append(trace)
    
    total_missing = 0
    total_remaining = 0
    total_consumed = 0
    total_produced = 0
    total_activities = 0
    
    for trace in traces:
        missing, remaining, consumed, produced = replay_trace(
            trace, net_struct, initial_marking_dict
        )
        total_missing += missing
        total_remaining += remaining
        total_consumed += consumed
        total_produced += produced
        total_activities += len(trace)
    
    if total_activities == 0:
        fitness = 1.0
    else:
        fitness = 1 - ((total_missing + total_remaining) / (2 * total_activities))
    
    fitness = max(0.0, min(1.0, fitness))
    
    return {
        "fitness": fitness,
        "total_traces": len(traces),
        "total_activities": total_activities,
        "total_missing_tokens": total_missing,
        "total_remaining_tokens": total_remaining,
        "total_consumed": total_consumed,
        "total_produced": total_produced
    }


# ============================================================================
# 3. SIMPLICITY
# ============================================================================

def calculate_simplicity(net):
    """Calculate simplicity: 1 / (1 + num_arcs)."""
    num_arcs = len(net.arcs)
    simplicity = 1 / (1 + num_arcs)
    return simplicity


# ============================================================================
# 4. COLLECT AND SAVE METRICS
# ============================================================================

def collect_metrics(df, net, initial_marking, final_marking):
    """
    Collect all metrics and return as a dictionary.
    """
    # Get fitness details
    fitness_details = calculate_fitness_details(df, net, initial_marking, final_marking)
    
    # Extract values
    fitness_score = fitness_details['fitness']
    simplicity_score = calculate_simplicity(net)
    precision_score = 1.0  # Placeholder until implemented
    
    # Overall score
    overall_score = 0.4 * fitness_score + 0.3 * precision_score + 0.3 * simplicity_score
    
    # F-score (harmonic mean)
    if fitness_score + precision_score > 0:
        f_score = 2 * (fitness_score * precision_score) / (fitness_score + precision_score)
    else:
        f_score = 0.0
    
    # Get activities from DataFrame
    case_col = 'case:concept:name'
    activity_col = 'concept:name'
    activities_list = sorted(df[activity_col].unique().tolist())
    
    # Build JSON structure
    metrics = {
        "overall_score": overall_score,
        "fitness_score": fitness_score,
        "simplicity_score": simplicity_score,
        "activities": activities_list,
        "algorithm": "inductive miner",
        "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
        "event_log": {
            "num_cases": int(df[case_col].nunique()),
            "num_events": len(df),
            "num_activities": len(activities_list)
        },
        "model_structure": {
            "num_places": len(net.places),
            "num_transitions": len(net.transitions),
            "num_arcs": len(net.arcs)
        },
        "quality_metrics": {
            "fitness_details": fitness_details,
            "precision_details": {
                "precision": precision_score
            },
            "f_score": f_score
        }
    }
    
    return metrics


def save_metrics(metrics, output_path="output/result_scores.json"):
    """
    Save metrics dictionary to JSON file.
    """
    import os
    
    output_dir = os.path.dirname(output_path)
    if output_dir and not os.path.exists(output_dir):
        os.makedirs(output_dir)
    
    with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
        json.dump(metrics, f, indent=2)
```

```python
    place_to_transitions = {}
    silent_transitions = set()

    for trans in net.transitions:
        input_arcs[trans] = []
        output_arcs[trans] = []
    
    # Extract arcs
    for arc in net.arcs:
        if hasattr(arc, 'source') and hasattr(arc, 'target'):
            source = arc.source
            target = arc.target
            
            if source in net.places and target in net.transitions:
                input_arcs[target].append(source)
            
            elif source in net.transitions and target in net.places:
                output_arcs[source].append(target)
    
    # Build place to transitions mapping
    for place in net.places:
        place_to_transitions[place] = []
        for trans in net.transitions:
            if place in input_arcs[trans]:
                place_to_transitions[place].append(trans)
    
    # Identify silent transitions
    for trans in net.transitions:
        if trans.label is None:

        'input_arcs': input_arcs,
        'output_arcs': output_arcs,

        'all_transitions': list(net.transitions)
    }

def enable_transitions(markings, net_struct):

    enabled = set()
    input_arcs = net_struct['input_arcs']
    
    for trans in net_struct['all_transitions']:
        input_places = input_arcs[trans]
        if all(markings.get(place, 0) > 0 for place in input_places):
            enabled.add(trans)
    
    return enabled


def fire_transition(markings, trans, net_struct):
    """Fire a transition: consume tokens from input, produce to output."""
    input_arcs = net_struct['input_arcs']
    output_arcs = net_struct['output_arcs']
    
    for place in input_arcs[trans]:
        markings[place] = markings.get(place, 0) - 1
    
    for place in output_arcs[trans]:
        markings[place] = markings.get(place, 0) + 1
    
    return markings


def fire_silent_transitions(markings, net_struct):
    """Fire all possible silent transitions until no more can fire."""
    silent = net_struct['silent_transitions']
    changed = True
    
    while changed:
        changed = False
        enabled = enable_transitions(markings, net_struct)
        
        for trans in enabled:
            if trans in silent:
                markings = fire_transition(markings, trans, net_struct)
                changed = True
                break
    
    return markings

    markings = initial_marking_dict.copy()
    missing_tokens = 0
    consumed = 0
    produced = 0

            consumed += len(net_struct['input_arcs'][trans])
            produced += len(net_struct['output_arcs'][trans])

                markings = fire_transition(markings, trans, net_struct)
                consumed += len(net_struct['input_arcs'][trans])
                produced += len(net_struct['output_arcs'][trans])
```

```python
        if tgt_idx is not None and src_pidx is not None:
            # Place -> Transition (input arc for transition)

    silent_trans = net_struct['silent_trans']

        while changed:

                        for pidx in input_arcs[tidx]:

                        for pidx in output_arcs[tidx]:

    - init_marking_list: initial marking as list
```

```python
import json
```

```python
# HIGH-PERFORMANCE DATA EXTRACTION (DETERMINISTIC - FIXED)
# ============================================================================

def extract_net_structure_fast(net):
    """
    Extract Petri net into pre-indexed Python structures for O(1) lookups.
    
    FIXED: All iterations sorted by name attribute for deterministic results.
    
    Creates:
    - input_arcs: list of lists (indexed by transition index)
    - output_arcs: list of lists (indexed by transition index)
    - place_to_trans: list of lists (indexed by place index)
    - label_to_trans: dict mapping label -> list of transition indices
    - silent_trans: set of transition indices with label None
    - all_places: list of place objects (sorted by name)
    - all_trans: list of transition objects (sorted by name)
    """
    # Sort transitions by name for deterministic indexing
    sorted_trans = sorted(net.transitions, key=lambda t: t.name if t.name else '')
    num_trans = len(sorted_trans)
    
    # Sort places by name for deterministic indexing
    sorted_places = sorted(net.places, key=lambda p: p.name if p.name else '')
    num_places = len(sorted_places)
    
    # Map objects to indices
    trans_to_idx = {t: i for i, t in enumerate(sorted_trans)}
    place_to_idx = {p: i for i, p in enumerate(sorted_places)}
    
    # Initialize arc lists
    input_arcs = [[] for _ in range(num_trans)]
    output_arcs = [[] for _ in range(num_trans)]
    place_to_trans = [[] for _ in range(num_places)]
    
    # Build arc structures
    for arc in net.arcs:
        src, tgt = arc.source, arc.target
        
        src_idx = trans_to_idx.get(src)
        tgt_idx = trans_to_idx.get(tgt)
        src_pidx = place_to_idx.get(src)
        tgt_pidx = place_to_idx.get(tgt)
        
        if src_idx is not None and tgt_pidx is not None:
            output_arcs[src_idx].append(tgt_pidx)
        
        if tgt_idx is not None and src_pidx is not None:
            input_arcs[tgt_idx].append(src_pidx)
            place_to_trans[src_pidx].append(tgt_idx)
    
    # Build label to transitions mapping
    label_to_trans = defaultdict(list)
    silent_trans = set()
    
    for i, trans in enumerate(sorted_trans):
        label = trans.label
        if label is None:
            silent_trans.add(i)
        else:
            label_to_trans[label].append(i)
    
    return {
        'input_arcs': input_arcs,
        'output_arcs': output_arcs,
        'place_to_trans': place_to_trans,
        'label_to_trans': dict(label_to_trans),
        'silent_trans': silent_trans,
        'all_places': sorted_places,
        'all_trans': sorted_trans,
        'num_trans': num_trans,
        'num_places': num_places
    }


# ============================================================================

def preprocess_log_fast(df):

    """
    case_col = 'case:concept:name'
    activity_col = 'concept:name'
    
    grouped = df.groupby(case_col)[activity_col].apply(list)
    traces = grouped.tolist()
    
    all_activities = set()

        all_activities.update(trace)
    
    case_info = {
        'num_cases': len(traces),
        'num_events': len(df),
        'num_activities': len(all_activities),
        'activities': sorted(list(all_activities)),
        'unique_traces': len(set(tuple(t) for t in traces))
    }
    
    return traces, case_info

# OPTIMIZED TOKEN-BASED REPLAY (FITNESS)
# ============================================================================

def fire_silent_transitions(marking, net_struct):
    """
    Fire all possible silent transitions until no more can fire.
    Uses changed flag for efficient iteration.
    """
    input_arcs = net_struct['input_arcs']
    output_arcs = net_struct['output_arcs']
    silent_trans = net_struct['silent_trans']
    num_trans = net_struct['num_trans']
    
    changed = True
    while changed:
        changed = False
        for tidx in range(num_trans):
            if tidx in silent_trans:
                enabled = True
                for pidx in input_arcs[tidx]:
                    if marking[pidx] < 1:
                        enabled = False
                        break
                
                if enabled:
                    for pidx in input_arcs[tidx]:
                        marking[pidx] -= 1
                    for pidx in output_arcs[tidx]:
                        marking[pidx] += 1
                    changed = True
                    break


def replay_trace_fast(trace, net_struct, init_marking_list):
    """
    Optimized trace replay with in-place state updates.
    """
    input_arcs = net_struct['input_arcs']
    output_arcs = net_struct['output_arcs']
    label_to_trans = net_struct['label_to_trans']
    silent_trans = net_struct['silent_trans']
    num_trans = net_struct['num_trans']
    
    marking = init_marking_list.copy()
    
    # Fire initial silent transitions
    fire_silent_transitions(marking, net_struct)
    
    missing = 0
    
    for activity in trace:
        trans_list = label_to_trans.get(activity)
        
        if not trans_list:
            missing += 1
            continue
        
        fired = False
        for tidx in trans_list:
            enabled = True
            for pidx in input_arcs[tidx]:
                if marking[pidx] < 1:
                    enabled = False
                    break
            
            if enabled:
                for pidx in input_arcs[tidx]:
                    marking[pidx] -= 1
                for pidx in output_arcs[tidx]:
                    marking[pidx] += 1
                fired = True
                break
        
        if not fired:
            missing += 1
        
        fire_silent_transitions(marking, net_struct)
    
    remaining = sum(marking)
    
    return missing, remaining


def calculate_fitness_fast(traces, net_struct, init_marking_list):
    """
    Calculate fitness for all traces.
    """
    total_missing = 0
    total_remaining = 0
    total_activities = 0
    
    for trace in traces:
        missing, remaining = replay_trace_fast(trace, net_struct, init_marking_list)
        total_missing += missing
        total_remaining += remaining
        total_activities += len(trace)
    
    if total_activities == 0:
        fitness = 1.0
    else:
        fitness = 1.0 - ((total_missing + total_remaining) / (2.0 * total_activities))
    
    fitness = max(0.0, min(1.0, fitness))
    
    return {
        'fitness': fitness,
        'total_traces': len(traces),
        'total_activities': total_activities,
        'total_missing_tokens': total_missing,
        'total_remaining_tokens': total_remaining
    }

def get_enabled_activity_labels(marking, net_struct):
    """
    Get set of activity labels for all enabled transitions.
    Excludes silent transitions (label is None).
    """
    input_arcs = net_struct['input_arcs']
    label_to_trans = net_struct['label_to_trans']
    silent_trans = net_struct['silent_trans']
    num_trans = net_struct['num_trans']
    
    enabled_labels = set()
    
    for tidx in range(num_trans):
        if tidx in silent_trans:
            continue
        
        enabled = True
        for pidx in input_arcs[tidx]:
            if marking[pidx] < 1:
                enabled = False
                break
        
        if enabled:
            # Find the label for this transition
            for label, trans_list in label_to_trans.items():
                if tidx in trans_list:
                    enabled_labels.add(label)
                    break
    
    return enabled_labels


def fire_transition_by_label(marking, net_struct, label):
    """
    Fire a transition by its activity label.
    Returns True if fired, False if not enabled.
    """
    input_arcs = net_struct['input_arcs']
    output_arcs = net_struct['output_arcs']
    label_to_trans = net_struct['label_to_trans']
    
    trans_list = label_to_trans.get(label)
    if not trans_list:
        return False
    
    for tidx in trans_list:
        enabled = True
        for pidx in input_arcs[tidx]:
            if marking[pidx] < 1:
                enabled = False
                break
        
        if enabled:
            for pidx in input_arcs[tidx]:
                marking[pidx] -= 1
            for pidx in output_arcs[tidx]:
                marking[pidx] += 1
            return True
    
    return False


def calculate_etc_precision(traces, net_struct, init_marking_list):
    """
    Calculate Escaping Edges Precision (ETC).
    
    For each activity in each trace:
    1. Collect enabled activity labels (excluding silent)
    2. Count escaping edges = enabled labels that are NOT the current activity
    3. Add to total_enabled and total_escaping
    4. Fire the matching transition if enabled
    5. Fire silent transitions
    
    Precision = 1 - (total_escaping / total_enabled)
    If total_enabled is 0, return 1.0
    """
    total_enabled = 0
    total_escaping = 0
    
    for trace in traces:
        marking = init_marking_list.copy()
        
        # Fire initial silent transitions
        fire_silent_transitions(marking, net_struct)
        
        for activity in trace:
            # Get enabled activity labels before firing
            enabled_labels = get_enabled_activity_labels(marking, net_struct)
            
            # Count escaping edges (enabled but not current activity)
            escaping = len(enabled_labels) - (1 if activity in enabled_labels else 0)
            
            total_enabled += len(enabled_labels)
            total_escaping += escaping
            
            # Fire the matching transition if enabled, else skip
            fired = fire_transition_by_label(marking, net_struct, activity)
            
            # Fire silent transitions
            fire_silent_transitions(marking, net_struct)
    
    # Calculate precision
    if total_enabled == 0:
        precision = 1.0
    else:
        precision = 1.0 - (float(total_escaping) / float(total_enabled))
    
    precision = max(0.0, min(1.0, precision))
    
    return {
        'precision': precision,
        'total_enabled': total_enabled,
        'total_escaping': total_escaping,
        'total_activities': sum(len(t) for t in traces)
    }

def calculate_simplicity_fast(net):
    """Calculate simplicity: 1 / (1 + num_arcs)."""
    num_arcs = len(net.arcs)
    return 1.0 / (1.0 + float(num_arcs))

    """
    Collect all metrics and return as a dictionary.
    """
    # Pre-process log once
    traces, case_info = preprocess_log_fast(df)

    precision_score = precision_details['precision']

    else:

    # Build JSON structure

        'activities': case_info['activities'],
        'algorithm': 'inductive miner',
```

# Building a Process Discovery Algorithm from Scratch

Great! I'm excited to help you build this step by step. Let me first explain the core concepts and logic before we write any code.

## What We're Building

We'll implement a **cut-based process discovery algorithm** (similar to the Inductive Miner). The goal is to take an event log and discover a **process tree** that represents the underlying workflow.

---

## Core Concepts

### 1. Event Log Structure
An event log contains:
- **Cases** (process instances)
- **Activities** (actions performed)
- **Timestamps** (when activities occurred)

Each case is a sequence of activities (a trace).

### 2. Directly Follows Relation
For each case, we track which activity directly follows another. This creates a **Directly Follows Graph (DFG)** showing all observed transitions.

### 3. The Cut-Based Discovery Approach

The algorithm works **recursively** using this logic:

```
1. Look at the current set of traces
2. Find a "cut" that splits the process into parts
3. Partition the traces based on that cut
4. Recursively discover each part
5. Combine results into a process tree
```

### 4. Types of Cuts (Process Operators)

| Operator | Symbol | Meaning | Example |
|----------|--------|---------|---------|
| **Sequence** | `→` | Activities happen in order | A → B → C |
| **Exclusive Choice** | `×` | One path OR another | A × B |
| **Parallel** | `∧` | Activities can happen in any order | A ∧ B |
| **Loop** | `⟳` | Body repeats with redo activities | ⟳(body, redo) |

### 5. How Partitioning Works

This is the **critical step**. Let me explain with an example:

**Suppose we have these traces:**
```
Case 1: [A, B, C]
Case 2: [A, B, C]
Case 3: [A, D, C]
Case 4: [A, D, C]
```

**Step 1: Build Directly Follows Graph**
```
A → B, A → D, B → C, D → C
```

**Step 2: Detect a Cut**
We notice:
- All traces start with **A**
- All traces end with **C**
- Between A and C, we have either **B** or **D** (never both)

This suggests an **exclusive choice cut**: `A → (B × D) → C`

**Step 3: Partition the Traces**
We split the middle section:
- Partition 1 (choice B): traces containing B
- Partition 2 (choice D): traces containing D

**Step 4: Recurse**
Apply the same logic to each partition until we reach base cases (single activity).

### 6. Recursion Base Cases

The recursion stops when:
- **Empty log**: Return empty tree
- **Single activity**: Return that activity as a leaf node
- **Single unique trace**: Return as sequence

---

## Algorithm Flow Diagram

```
                    [Full Event Log]
                           │
                           ▼
              ┌─────────────────────────┐
              │   Build DFG & Analyze   │
              └─────────────────────────┘
                           │
                           ▼
              ┌─────────────────────────┐
              │    Find Best Cut        │ ← (Sequence/Choice/Parallel/Loop)
              └─────────────────────────┘
                           │
                           ▼
              ┌─────────────────────────┐
              │   Partition Traces      │ ← Split log based on cut
              └─────────────────────────┘
                           │
           ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
           ▼               ▼               ▼
     [Partition 1]   [Partition 2]   [Partition N]
           │               │               │
           └───────────────┴───────────────┘
                           │
                           ▼ (Recurse on each)
                    [Process Tree]
```

---

## What We'll Build Step-by-Step

| Step | Component | Purpose |
|------|-----------|---------|
| 1 | Data Loading | Read .xes with pm4py, convert to DataFrame |
| 2 | Trace Extraction | Convert DataFrame to list of traces |
| 3 | DFG Construction | Build directly-follows graph |
| 4 | Cut Detection | Find sequence/choice/parallel/loop cuts |
| 5 | Partitioning | Split traces based on detected cut |
| 6 | Recursion | Apply discovery to each partition |
| 7 | Process Tree | Build and return final tree structure |

---

Let me know your preferences, and I'll guide you through the first implementation step with full explanations! 🚀

# Step 2: Building the Directly-Follows Graph

## What This Code Does (Logic Explanation)

### Goal
Build three outputs from the DataFrame:
1. **Arcs**: Set of `(A, B)` tuples where activity B immediately follows activity A in any trace
2. **Start Activities**: Set of activities that appear first in any case
3. **End Activities**: Set of activities that appear last in any case

### Key Constraint
**No row-by-row iteration** - all operations must be vectorized using Pandas `groupby`, `shift()`, or similar.

---

### Logic Breakdown

#### 1. Start Activities
```
For each unique case:
  → Get the FIRST activity in that case
  → Collect all unique first activities into a set
```
**Vectorized approach**: `groupby('case:concept:name')['concept:name'].first()`
- Groups all rows by case ID
- Takes the first activity value from each group
- Converts to set for uniqueness

#### 2. End Activities
```
For each unique case:
  → Get the LAST activity in that case
  → Collect all unique last activities into a set
```
**Vectorized approach**: `groupby('case:concept:name')['concept:name'].last()`
- Same grouping, but takes the last activity value from each group

#### 3. Directly-Follows Arcs
```
For each row in the DataFrame:
  → Look at the NEXT row's activity
  → Check if BOTH rows belong to the SAME case
  → If yes, create arc: (current_activity, next_activity)
```

**The Challenge**: How do we get "next activity" without looping?

**Vectorized Solution Using `shift()`**:
```
Original:  [A, B, C, D, E, F]
Shifted:   [B, C, D, E, F, NaN]  ← shifted up by 1

Row 0: current=A, next=B  → arc (A,B)
Row 1: current=B, next=C  → arc (B,C)
...
```

But we must ensure "next" is within the **same case**. So we:
1. Create a `next_activity` column using `shift(-1)`
2. Create a `next_case` column using `shift(-1)` on case ID
3. Filter: keep only rows where `current_case == next_case`
4. Extract unique `(activity, next_activity)` pairs

---

## The Code

```python
def build_directly_follows_graph(df):
    """
    Build the directly-follows graph from the event log DataFrame.
    
    Uses ONLY vectorized Pandas operations - no row iteration.
    
    Parameters:
        df: Pandas DataFrame with columns 'case:concept:name' and 'concept:name'
            Rows must be in chronological order (as loaded from .xes file)
    
    Returns:
        arcs: set of tuples (A, B) where B directly follows A in some trace
        start_activities: set of activities that start traces
        end_activities: set of activities that end traces
    """
    
    case_col = 'case:concept:name'
    activity_col = 'concept:name'
    
    # ============================================================
    # START ACTIVITIES: First activity of each case
    # ============================================================
    # groupby groups all rows by case ID
    # .first() takes the first activity value from each group
    # This is fully vectorized - operates on entire column at once
    start_activities = set(df.groupby(case_col)[activity_col].first())
    
    # ============================================================
    # END ACTIVITIES: Last activity of each case  
    # ============================================================
    # Same logic, but .last() takes the last activity from each group
    end_activities = set(df.groupby(case_col)[activity_col].last())
    
    # ============================================================
    # DIRECTLY-FOLLOWS ARCS: (A, B) pairs within same case
    # ============================================================
    
    # Create a working copy to avoid modifying original DataFrame
    df_work = df.copy()
    
    # Shift activity column UP by 1 to get the "next" activity for each row
    # Row i's 'next_activity' = Row (i+1)'s 'concept:name'
    df_work['next_activity'] = df_work[activity_col].shift(-1)
    
    # Shift case column UP by 1 to check if next row is same case
    df_work['next_case'] = df_work[case_col].shift(-1)
    
    # CRITICAL FILTER: Only keep arcs where next activity is in SAME case
    # This prevents creating arcs across case boundaries
    same_case_mask = df_work[case_col] == df_work['next_case']
    df_valid_arcs = df_work[same_case_mask]
    
    # Create arc set from (current_activity, next_activity) pairs
    # zip() creates tuples, set() ensures uniqueness
    arcs = set(zip(df_valid_arcs[activity_col], df_valid_arcs['next_activity']))
    
    return arcs, start_activities, end_activities
```

## What This Code Does (Logic Explanation)

### Goal
Build three outputs from the DataFrame:
1. **Arcs**: Set of `(A, B)` tuples where activity B immediately follows activity A in any trace
2. **Start Activities**: Set of activities that appear first in any case
3. **End Activities**: Set of activities that appear last in any case

### Key Constraint
**No row-by-row iteration** - all operations must be vectorized using Pandas `groupby`, `shift()`, or similar.

---

### Logic Breakdown

#### 1. Start Activities
```
For each unique case:
  → Get the FIRST activity in that case
  → Collect all unique first activities into a set
```
**Vectorized approach**: `groupby('case:concept:name')['concept:name'].first()`
- Groups all rows by case ID
- Takes the first activity value from each group
- Converts to set for uniqueness

#### 2. End Activities
```
For each unique case:
  → Get the LAST activity in that case
  → Collect all unique last activities into a set
```
**Vectorized approach**: `groupby('case:concept:name')['concept:name'].last()`
- Same grouping, but takes the last activity value from each group

#### 3. Directly-Follows Arcs
```
For each row in the DataFrame:
  → Look at the NEXT row's activity
  → Check if BOTH rows belong to the SAME case
  → If yes, create arc: (current_activity, next_activity)
```

**The Challenge**: How do we get "next activity" without looping?

**Vectorized Solution Using `shift()`**:
```
Original:  [A, B, C, D, E, F]
Shifted:   [B, C, D, E, F, NaN]  ← shifted up by 1

Row 0: current=A, next=B  → arc (A,B)
Row 1: current=B, next=C  → arc (B,C)
...
```

But we must ensure "next" is within the **same case**. So we:
1. Create a `next_activity` column using `shift(-1)`
2. Create a `next_case` column using `shift(-1)` on case ID
3. Filter: keep only rows where `current_case == next_case`
4. Extract unique `(activity, next_activity)` pairs

```python
def build_directly_follows_graph(df):
    """
    Build the directly-follows graph from the event log DataFrame.
    
    Uses ONLY vectorized Pandas operations - no row iteration.
    
    Parameters:
        df: Pandas DataFrame with columns 'case:concept:name' and 'concept:name'
            Rows must be in chronological order (as loaded from .xes file)
    
    Returns:
        arcs: set of tuples (A, B) where B directly follows A in some trace
        start_activities: set of activities that start traces
        end_activities: set of activities that end traces
    """
    
    case_col = 'case:concept:name'
    activity_col = 'concept:name'
    
    # ============================================================
    # START ACTIVITIES: First activity of each case
    # ============================================================
    # groupby groups all rows by case ID
    # .first() takes the first activity value from each group
    # This is fully vectorized - operates on entire column at once
    start_activities = set(df.groupby(case_col)[activity_col].first())
    
    # ============================================================
    # END ACTIVITIES: Last activity of each case  
    # ============================================================
    # Same logic, but .last() takes the last activity from each group
    end_activities = set(df.groupby(case_col)[activity_col].last())
    
    # ============================================================
    # DIRECTLY-FOLLOWS ARCS: (A, B) pairs within same case
    # ============================================================
    
    # Create a working copy to avoid modifying original DataFrame
    df_work = df.copy()
    
    # Shift activity column UP by 1 to get the "next" activity for each row
    # Row i's 'next_activity' = Row (i+1)'s 'concept:name'
    df_work['next_activity'] = df_work[activity_col].shift(-1)
    
    # Shift case column UP by 1 to check if next row is same case
    df_work['next_case'] = df_work[case_col].shift(-1)
    
    # CRITICAL FILTER: Only keep arcs where next activity is in SAME case
    # This prevents creating arcs across case boundaries
    same_case_mask = df_work[case_col] == df_work['next_case']
    df_valid_arcs = df_work[same_case_mask]
    
    # Create arc set from (current_activity, next_activity) pairs
    # zip() creates tuples, set() ensures uniqueness
    arcs = set(zip(df_valid_arcs[activity_col], df_valid_arcs['next_activity']))
    
    return arcs, start_activities, end_activities
```

```python
def parse_sample_data(raw_text):
    """
    Parse whitespace-separated raw text into a Pandas DataFrame.
    
    Uses io.StringIO to wrap text, then pd.read_csv with regex separator.
    No manual list creation - parses directly from text.
    """
    # Wrap raw text in StringIO object (makes it file-like for read_csv)
    buffer = io.StringIO(raw_text)
    
    # Read with whitespace separator (\s+ matches one or more spaces/tabs)
    # engine='python' required for regex separators
    df = pd.read_csv(buffer, sep=r'\s+', engine='python')
    
    # Strip any leading/trailing spaces from column names
    df.columns = df.columns.str.strip()
    
    # Strip any leading/trailing spaces from string values in both columns
    for col in df.columns:
        if df[col].dtype == 'object':
            df[col] = df[col].str.strip()
    
    return df

def build_directly_follows_graph(df):
    """
    Build the directly-follows graph from the event log DataFrame.
    
    Uses ONLY vectorized Pandas operations - no row iteration.
    
    Parameters:
        df: Pandas DataFrame with columns 'case:concept:name' and 'concept:name'
            Rows must be in chronological order (as loaded from .xes file)
    
    Returns:
        arcs: set of tuples (A, B) where B directly follows A in some trace
        start_activities: set of activities that start traces
        end_activities: set of activities that end traces
    """
    
    case_col = 'case:concept:name'
    activity_col = 'concept:name'
    
    # ============================================================
    # START ACTIVITIES: First activity of each case
    # ============================================================
    # groupby groups all rows by case ID
    # .first() takes the first activity value from each group
    # This is fully vectorized - operates on entire column at once
    start_activities = set(df.groupby(case_col)[activity_col].first())
    
    # ============================================================
    # END ACTIVITIES: Last activity of each case  
    # ============================================================
    # Same logic, but .last() takes the last activity from each group
    end_activities = set(df.groupby(case_col)[activity_col].last())
    
    # ============================================================
    # DIRECTLY-FOLLOWS ARCS: (A, B) pairs within same case
    # ============================================================
    
    # Create a working copy to avoid modifying original DataFrame
    df_work = df.copy()
    
    # Shift activity column UP by 1 to get the "next" activity for each row
    # Row i's 'next_activity' = Row (i+1)'s 'concept:name'
    df_work['next_activity'] = df_work[activity_col].shift(-1)
    
    # Shift case column UP by 1 to check if next row is same case
    df_work['next_case'] = df_work[case_col].shift(-1)
    
    # CRITICAL FILTER: Only keep arcs where next activity is in SAME case
    # This prevents creating arcs across case boundaries
    same_case_mask = df_work[case_col] == df_work['next_case']
    df_valid_arcs = df_work[same_case_mask]
    
    # Create arc set from (current_activity, next_activity) pairs
    # zip() creates tuples, set() ensures uniqueness
    arcs = set(zip(df_valid_arcs[activity_col], df_work.loc[same_case_mask, 'next_activity']))
    
    return arcs, start_activities, end_activities


# Run the graph building function
arcs, start_activities, end_activities = build_directly_follows_graph(df_sample)
```

```python
    # engine='python' required for regex separators
    df = pd.read_csv(buffer, sep=r'\s+', engine='python')
    
    # Strip any leading/trailing spaces from column names
    df.columns = df.columns.str.strip()

def build_directly_follows_graph(df):
    """
    Build the directly-follows graph from the event log DataFrame.
    
    Uses ONLY vectorized Pandas operations - no row iteration.
    
    Parameters:
        df: Pandas DataFrame with columns 'case:concept:name' and 'concept:name'
            Rows must be in chronological order (as loaded from .xes file)
    
    Returns:
        arcs: set of tuples (A, B) where B directly follows A in some trace
        start_activities: set of activities that start traces
        end_activities: set of activities that end traces
    """
    
    case_col = 'case:concept:name'
    activity_col = 'concept:name'
    
    # ============================================================
    # START ACTIVITIES: First activity of each case
    # ============================================================
    # groupby groups all rows by case ID
    # .first() takes the first activity value from each group
    # This is fully vectorized - operates on entire column at once
    start_activities = set(df.groupby(case_col)[activity_col].first())
    
    # ============================================================
    # END ACTIVITIES: Last activity of each case  
    # ============================================================
    # Same logic, but .last() takes the last activity from each group
    end_activities = set(df.groupby(case_col)[activity_col].last())
    
    # ============================================================
    # DIRECTLY-FOLLOWS ARCS: (A, B) pairs within same case
    # ============================================================
    
    # Create a working copy to avoid modifying original DataFrame
    df_work = df.copy()
    
    # Shift activity column UP by 1 to get the "next" activity for each row
    # Row i's 'next_activity' = Row (i+1)'s 'concept:name'
    df_work['next_activity'] = df_work[activity_col].shift(-1)
    
    # Shift case column UP by 1 to check if next row is same case
    df_work['next_case'] = df_work[case_col].shift(-1)
    
    # CRITICAL FILTER: Only keep arcs where next activity is in SAME case
    # This prevents creating arcs across case boundaries
    same_case_mask = df_work[case_col] == df_work['next_case']
    df_valid_arcs = df_work[same_case_mask]
    
    # Create arc set from (current_activity, next_activity) pairs
    # zip() creates tuples, set() ensures uniqueness
    arcs = set(zip(df_valid_arcs[activity_col], df_work.loc[same_case_mask, 'next_activity']))
    
    return arcs, start_activities, end_activities


# Run the graph building function
```

```python
import pandas as pd
import io

def parse_sample_data(raw_text):
    """
    Parse whitespace-separated raw text into a Pandas DataFrame.
    
    Uses manual line-by-line parsing to handle activity names with spaces.
    Splits each line on the FIRST whitespace only:
      - Part 1: case ID (no spaces)
      - Part 2: activity name (may contain spaces)
    
    Parameters:
        raw_text: String containing the raw event log data
    
    Returns:
        df: Pandas DataFrame with columns 'case:concept:name' and 'concept:name'
    """
    # Split raw text into individual lines
    lines = raw_text.strip().split('\n')
    
    # Prepare lists to hold parsed data
    case_ids = []
    activities = []
    
    # Skip the header line (index 0), process only data lines
    for line in lines[1:]:
        # Strip leading/trailing whitespace from the line
        line = line.strip()
        
        # Skip empty lines if any
        if not line:
            continue
        
        # CRITICAL: Split on FIRST whitespace only (maxsplit=1)
        # None means any whitespace (space, tab, etc.)
        # This ensures activity names with spaces stay intact
        parts = line.split(None, 1)
        
        # Extract case ID (first part) and activity name (second part)
        case_id = parts[0]
        activity_name = parts[1] if len(parts) > 1 else ''
        
        case_ids.append(case_id)
        activities.append(activity_name)
    
    # Build DataFrame with exactly 2 columns
    df = pd.DataFrame({
        'case:concept:name': case_ids,
        'concept:name': activities
    })
    
    return df
```

**What we're looking for:** A main body of the process with one or more "return paths" that loop back.

1. Identify candidate main group (must include all starts and ends)

3. Verify return groups have no internal arcs between them
4. Verify arcs to/from return groups follow loop pattern

```python
    # ============================================================
```

```python
    # -----------------------------------------------------------

    # -----------------------------------------------------------
    has_enter_loop = any(a in main_group and b in return_candidates for a, b in arcs)
    has_exit_loop = any(a in return_candidates and b in main_group for a, b in arcs)
    
    if not (has_enter_loop and has_exit_loop):

    # All validations passed - return the structure
    # ============================================================
    return (main_group, return_groups)
```

```python
    topologically ordered.

        List of sets (ordered groups) if 2+ SCCs found, else None

    # Get all unique activities

    for a, b in arcs:

        all_activities.add(b)
    
    if len(all_activities) < 2:
```
